claim: P-615 (frequentist NMA, 53 RCTs / 4582 participants) reported digital reminiscence therapy ranked best for cognitive function (SUCRA 93.6%) and depressive symptoms (SUCRA 94.9%), with individual best for QoL (98.3%) and group best for adherence (95.6%).
second_reader_note: Block "What are the outcomes? (Results)" matches every number in the record ("53 RCTs involving 4582 participants"; "Digital reminiscence therapy ranked best for cognitive function (SMD 5.02 vs treatment-as-usual; SUCRA 93.6%) and depressive symptoms (SUCRA 94.9%). Individual ... quality of life (SUCRA 98.3%). Group ... adherence (SUCRA 95.6%)"), so the evidence is real, but it bounds the prior only for cognition and depressive-symptom outcomes: in-person formats (individual, group) still rank best for QoL and adherence, the block never says digital delivery was "solitary" or tests the interpersonal-engagement mechanism, it frames the prior state as "unclear" rather than a settled belief, and it pools dementia+MCI with wide CIs/transitivity caveats (the record's own clinical_implication concedes "no belief-reversal established"). Narrower scope: digital delivery is not inferior to in-person delivery for cognitive and depressive outcomes in a pooled dementia/MCI SUCRA ranking, while in-person formats remain best for QoL and adherence.

claim: P-224 compared corneal confocal microscopy (CCM) nerve metrics against MRI hippocampal/whole-brain volumetry for MCI-to-dementia progression in a longitudinal cohort (N=107). CCM (72-75%) modestly edged MRI (68-69%) - an overlapping margin that CHALLENGES (does not disprove) MRI as the best single-modality prognostic biomarker.
second_reader_note: P-224's block (title "Corneal nerve loss predicts dementia in patients with mild cognitive impairment", content consistent with title) is a within-study head-to-head: "Among 107 MCI participants, 33 (30.8%) progressed to dementia over about 2.6 years ... CCM prognostic accuracy was reported higher than hippocampal/whole-brain volumetry (about 72-75% vs 68-69%)" and Key findings "CCM measures outperformed hippocampal and whole-brain volumetry in this cohort for progression prediction" - every number in the record (N=107, 72-75% vs 68-69%, longitudinal, MCI-to-dementia) matches. The prior (MRI hippocampal volumetry as the best single-modality prognostic marker for MCI conversion) is a genuine field-level assumption, and the record already scopes itself to a single cohort with a modest margin ("challenges, does not disprove", "requires replication"), so no narrower rescope is needed; the only interpretive phrase not in the block ("overlapping margin", no CIs given) weakens rather than inflates the claim.

claim: saliency no attention analysis no feature-importance ranking beyond the variable-combination search itself
second_reader_note: P-788 is a 59-patient clinical/plasma p-tau181 prognostic study in oldest-old MCI (MMSE, CDT, Lawton in an RPDPM, AUC 0.945; p-tau181 AUC 0.57); the block declares "C1 = Neuroimaging is rejected ... No MRI, fMRI, DTI, PET ... described anywhere" and contains no mention of corpus callosum, white matter, or any volumetric measure, so nothing in it bounds or contradicts the prior "Corpus callosum volumetric loss is the earliest detectable white matter MCI signal". The what_disproved_it field is a verbatim fragment of the block's XAI-absence sentence ("no saliency, no attention analysis, no feature-importance ranking beyond the variable-combination search itself"), which describes what the paper lacks, not evidence against any assumption. The block's title matches its content (not misattached); the record is simply unsupported.

claim: P-281 (Audronyte 2023; single-site, cross-sectional, N=90 = 30 CN / 30 MCI-AD / 30 mild-dementia-AD): olfactory recognition memory was significantly impaired in AD dementia but MCI-AD did NOT differ significantly from CN, while verbal memory WAS already impaired at MCI-AD. In this small cross-sectional cohort olfactory recognition-memory deficits were not detected at the prodromal (MCI-AD) stage - a null in 30/group ...
second_reader_note: P-281 block (title "Olfactory memory in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease", Audronyte et al. 2023, Frontiers in Neurology) states under Outcomes: "Olfactory immediate and delayed recognition were significantly lower in the mild dementia group than in MCI-AD and CN groups. MCI-AD and CN did not differ significantly on olfactory memory. Verbal memory was impaired in both MCI-AD and mild dementia compared with CN" - a within-study null at the prodromal stage with a within-study positive comparator, exactly as the record claims; sample "90 participants divided evenly across CN, MCI-AD, and MD-AD groups" (= 30/group), "Cross-sectional", "Single-center design", "Only one olfactory memory paradigm was used", Sniffin' Sticks, all match the record's numbers and scope caveats. The prior is anchored in the block itself ("determine whether olfactory memory changes are present already in the prodromal stage of AD"; "Supports literature suggesting olfactory impairment is an AD marker"), so it is a real field-level assumption applied to the recognition-memory sub-construct rather than a straw man, and the record already restricts the disproof to this one paradigm and small cross-sectional cohort, so no further rescoping is needed; registry row confirms study_design_type=cross_sectional, N=90, no duplicate_of.

claim: Grad-CAM saliency in P-10 (DuCAN, N=390 retinal fundus+OCT) indicated the optic nerve head did not contribute as much as expected, with the model instead focusing on vascular features - a model-specific saliency observation, not a definitive refutation of ONH biomarker value.
second_reader_note: Within-study null on ONH is present: P-10 block ("What can be improved?") says "the optic nerve head (ONH) did not contribute as much as expected" and its Results say Grad-CAM showed the model focused on "vascular features for MCI/AD"; the canonical P-5 block ("What are the problems?") says "changes in the optic nerve head were not used to discriminate MCI patients", with N=390 (117+273) and Grad-CAM matching in both blocks and the registry. The prior is one the authors themselves held ("as expected"), and the record already confines the bound to a model-specific saliency observation in one small cohort, so no narrower scope is needed. Hygiene only: the narrative and `paper` field cite P-10, which is a STUB-DEDUP of P-5 marked "must not be cited as evidence"; the citation should read P-5 throughout.

claim: Corpus-wide absence: out-of-scope (non-mci) api-call graph extraction, gvae dimensionality reduction, rfe/fs feature selection, lightgbm and svm classification. modality never applied to T4 (T4) despite appearing in corpus for other tasks.
second_reader_note: The record's "modality" field is not a modality at all but the verbatim Key_Methods string of one registry row (P-206, Modality = "out-of-scope (non-MCI)"), whose summary block is an Android malware-detection paper ("Malware detection framework based on graph variational autoencoder extracted embeddings from API-call graphs"; block states "This study is not in Alzheimer/MCI domain"). A gap demanding that API-call-graph/GVAE/LightGBM malware methods be applied to T4 is out of scope (not MCI), papers_claiming_gap is UNRESOLVED, and the "1 papers use ... modality" evidence is a single-row keyword-combination artefact, so it fails the rule on both the out-of-scope and artefact grounds.

claim: saliency no attention analysis no feature-importance ranking beyond the variable-combination search itself
second_reader_note: P-788's block (title matches: oldest-old MCI cohort, 59 patients from a Zaragoza geriatrics outpatient clinic, RPDPM on Lawton+MMSE+CDT, AUC 0.945) is not a CHF-patient study and contains no ejection fraction or cardiac output measurement; heart failure appears only as a medical-history checklist row (9.4% sMCI vs 29.6% pMCI, p = 0.047) that the block says "never enters any model" and which, if anything, associates HF with progression rather than contradicting a cardiac-feature prior. The what_disproved_it text is a verbatim fragment of the block's XAI-absence sentence ("no SHAP, no LIME, no saliency, no attention analysis, no feature-importance ranking beyond the variable-combination search itself"; "XAI_Method: none"), i.e. a statement that no interpretability method was used, not evidence against any prior. The prior belief is a straw man for this paper and the claimed disproving evidence does not exist in the block.

claim: Disease-specific MCI biomarkers are non-generalizable; MCI in context of comorbidity follows different pathway than amnestic/primary MCI
second_reader_note: Both findings misread their blocks: P-19's "What did the authors do?" is "machine learning models to predict MCI risk among occupational dust-exposed miners" (registry Modality Clinical/tabular, population_specificity occupational_exposure), with no CHF and no corpus callosum/white-matter content; P-35 is the CHF study ("predict MCI risk in patients with chronic heart failure") but its key predictors are "psychosocial adaptation management, age, FT3, depression score, hemoglobin, sleep duration, and gender", and neither block mentions Parkinson's disease, substantia nigra, dopamine, or any imaging. With both anchor findings absent from the evidence, the combined insight ("disease-specific MCI biomarkers are non-generalizable") is an unsupported boilerplate statement rather than a joint inference from these two tabular ML risk-prediction papers.

claim: Graph-based representations of brain connectivity outperform regional feature vectors for MCI classification
second_reader_note: Only two supporters are listed (P-14, P-75), so the three-study minimum cannot be met; both are ADNI (registry Dataset=ADNI, contradicting dataset_families=2) and both are GCN pipelines (Architecture_Family=A5, contradicting method_families=3). Neither block contains the comparison as written: P-14's "What has been done?" says prior work used "FC-only or SC-only features, high-dimensional handcrafted selections, and standard GCN/kernel models" and its significance is "stronger MCI discrimination than simpler graph or single-modality pipelines" (a multimodal-fusion and multi-scale claim, not graph-vs-regional-vector); P-75 says existing approaches "use lower-order networks or less expressive graph learners" and reports gains "versus several existing methods", i.e. higher-order graph vs lower-order graph, never graph vs regional feature vectors.

claim: Reaction-time / temporal-dynamic features are used as MCI-discriminative signals across modalities (computerized testing, driving, EEG+HRV, speech). NOTE: only P-101 shows WITHIN-STUDY that temporal features add information BEYOND accuracy-only scoring; the rest report temporal features without that comparison, so the "beyond accuracy-only" claim rests on 1 paper, not the consensus.
second_reader_note: Supported as written only for computerized testing and speech: P-101 ("Key Predictors: Response accuracy, reaction time"; "Reaction time features complementary to accuracy scores for MCI discrimination"), P-58 ("temporal hesitation-related speech features ... can detect MCI") and P-59 (posterior-thresholding hesitation features, "retaining discriminative signal"), but P-58/P-59 share a group and corpus family (both "BEA 116 pretrain", Hungarian cohorts) so speech is one independent line. P-83's block lists only "Time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear feature extraction from EEG/HRV" with the finding attributed to multimodal fusion, not to any temporal/reaction-time feature, and P-69's block names "driving asymmetry/turning and hard-braking" predictors from "31 driving time-series variables" with no reaction-time feature. Narrower scope: temporal/reaction-time features are MCI-discriminative in computerized testing (P-101) and speech (P-58/P-59, non-independent), with driving (P-69) only as time-series behaviour; drop EEG+HRV from the modality list and keep the beyond-accuracy claim pinned to P-101.

claim: P-221 ran a direct head-to-head comparison in PD: a clinical+gait model reached >80% accuracy/specificity, while ADDING amyloid PET did NOT improve and 'often weakened' prediction. CRITICAL CAVEAT: the PET subgroup is severely underpowered (n=36: 19 PD-MCI + 17 non-PD-MCI) - this null is better read as 'insufficient power to detect a modest PET benefit' than as proven absence of incremental value.
second_reader_note: P-221's block (title "Machine learning can predict mild cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease", cohort "75 PD participants (33 PD-MCI, 42 noPD-MCI)", PET subgroup "19 PD-MCI, 17 noPD-MCI") states in Outcomes that clinical+gait Model 1 reached "accuracy/specificity above 80%" and "Adding amyloid PET features reduced performance", with Key findings verbatim "amyloid PET did not improve and in this study often weakened prediction" - a within-study reversal that matches every number and quote in the record. The prior is already scoped to PD-MCI ML classification and the record itself carries the underpowering caveat (PET n=36) and the "thematic support, not standalone" framing, so no further rescope is needed; the assumption is a real one because the paper's stated aim was to "test amyloid PET utility for PD-MCI prediction".

claim: Ocular channels (retinal structure and eye-movement behavior) are repeatedly supported as scalable biomarker directions for early cognitive decline detection
second_reader_note: Four independent blocks support the statement as written across both ocular channels: P-5 ("potential of using retinal imaging as a non-invasive, accessible biomarker for early MCI detection", fundus+OCT DL, N=390), P-952 ("fundus-photography-based screening approach for MCI recognition in community and clinical settings", SVM AUC 0.87, N=86), P-105 ("ET-based screening could become scalable, low-burden early detection for cognitive decline", eye-tracking review), and P-966 ("Supports oculomotor inhibitory-control testing as an objective, low-cost MCI screening channel", N=249 Korean cohort) - three-plus dataset families and method families, no contradiction. P-109 should be struck from supporting_papers: its block is a paraphrase of P-105 (same metrics/paradigms/"Published in Information Fusion") while its own sample field says "1075 (390 AD/370 MCI/315 HC), sMRI", so it is misattached or a duplicate and not independent support; the finding stands without it.

claim: P-581 (Torso 2025; single NACC cohort, N=826, diffusion MRI, Kaplan-Meier survival): cortical minicolumn-related diffusivity (PerpPD+ in medial-temporal and connected regions) outperformed hippocampal volume, cortical volume, and cortical thickness in predicting faster MCI-to-dementia conversion (single-cohort, proprietary pipeline, no external validation, qualitative survival separation with no reported HR/AUC).
second_reader_note: The P-581 block (Torso et al. 2025, Alzheimer's & Dementia, NACC, N=826, T2/V2, Kaplan-Meier) states in "Key findings reported": "Cortical diffusivity (PerpPD+, medial-temporal and connected regions) outperforms hippocampal volume, cortical volume, and cortical thickness in Kaplan-Meier survival, predicting faster MCI-to-dementia conversion", and its comparisons field explicitly says it "challenges the primacy of hippocampal volume as the best single structural prognostic marker for conversion" — a within-study head-to-head that bounds a genuine field-level prior, with all numbers (826, 2025, NACC) and caveats (no AUC, proprietary Oxford Brain Diagnostics pipeline, no external validation) matching the block. The record already self-scopes to the single NACC cohort, so no further rescoping is needed; the only element not literally in the block is the "no HR" half of the "no reported HR/AUC" caveat (the block says only "no AUC"), which is a hedge rather than an evidential claim.

claim: Explainable AI (XAI) methods in MCI research rely on descriptive feature attribution (SHAP, Grad-CAM, attention maps) without prospective evidence that these explanations provide actionable clinical reasoning or measurably improve clinician decision-making.
second_reader_note: The gap statement is a well-formed, MCI-relevant absence and no listed block contains a prospective clinician study or decision-quality endpoint (P-81 even states "Needs broader replication and stronger prospective evaluation"), but the record's evidence_for_open_status claims "XAI applications in the corpus (P-54, P-81, P-82, P-90, P-92) generate post-hoc attribution maps", and the P-54, P-90 and P-92 blocks contain no XAI method at all (registry XAI_Method = none for all three; P-90 is a narrative review of ginseng, Task_Type T6). Narrower supportable form: the gap stands grounded only on P-81 (saliency/Grad-CAM) and P-82 (occlusion analysis); P-54, P-90, P-92 must be dropped from the grounding list and the "verified corpus-wide absence" wording cannot be checked from the listed papers.

claim: EEG-ML MCI-detection studies report headline accuracies of 93-99.95% obtained under segment/epoch/spectrogram-image-level cross-validation that splits a single subject's autocorrelated epochs across folds (leaking subject identity), yet no study runs the controlled comparison of identical models under segment-wise vs subject-wise CV on the SAME data to isolate the leakage-attributable inflation.
second_reader_note: The absence itself is open: no block among the ten describes a within-study comparison of identical models under segment-wise vs subject-wise CV (P-12 "Subject-based 5-fold CV" 70.11%, P-129 "cross-subject validation scheme" 90.97%, P-153 "41 subjects ... for training ... 20 subjects ... for test ... voting on the labels of the timepieces of each test subject" 93.96%, P-501 LOO 91.97% are subject-level results only, never contrasted with segment-level folds). But the premise overreaches: the 93% floor is P-153, whose block describes subject-level splits, i.e. the opposite of the stated mechanism, and the P-121/P-112/P-119 blocks state N and accuracy but never the CV unit; only P-31 ("9720 segmented samples", 10-fold CV, "leakage risks must be scrutinized") and P-70 (segmentation + 5-fold CV, "Subject-independent validation" listed under What can be improved) evidence non-subject-wise CV. Narrower scope: anchor the segment-level premise on P-31/P-70 (same 27-subject public set, 95.5-99.95%), cite P-121/P-112/P-119 only as tiny-N near-ceiling results with unstated CV unit (P-112/P-119 are also three-class staging, T3), and keep P-153/P-129/P-12 on the subject-wise contrast side; the closure criterion remains fully open.

claim: EEG/MEG network- and connectivity-based MCI discrimination is reported almost entirely on single-site, small-N cohorts (mostly group-difference studies, few actual classifiers); the cross-site external validity of these network biomarkers (train one site, test an independent site/scanner/montage) is not quantified anywhere in this corpus for models built on network/connectivity/graph features (raw-signal end-to-end ...
second_reader_note: No listed paper closes the gap: the three connectivity/graph-feature studies are single-cohort with no independent-site test (P-553 "Sample N: 25 — 12 MCI / 13 HC", "no classifier"; P-463 "acquired at only two Japanese hospitals", "purely group-difference analysis"; P-501 "leave-one-out ... K=10,5,3" on a "single-population (older Black American) cohort"), P-480/P-447 report no classifier, and P-499 states "No external/multi-site validation" while using spectral/Hjorth not network features. The only cross-site EEG study, P-62, is a raw-signal CNN whose block confirms "model training on overt dementia classes" with MCI "bACC about 0.715 in one setting", exactly as the record carves out; every number and characterisation in evidence_for_open_status matches its block, and the closure criteria are concrete and MCI-specific.

claim: Default Mode Network disruption is the dominant functional connectivity biomarker across MCI stages
second_reader_note: Only one supporting paper (P-97) is listed, so the rule's floor of three independent supporters from more than one dataset and method family cannot be met, and the card's dataset_families=2 / method_families=3 counts cannot be derived from a one-paper list. P-97's block is a single ADNI rs-fMRI Node2Vec study (N=125: 36 HC/30 EMCI/33 LMCI/26 AD) whose "Key findings reported" says "DMN and DAN networks most important for classification" and "DMN and DAN consistently showed high discriminative importance" - i.e. DMN shares importance with DAN, so even this lone supporter does not show DMN as "the dominant" connectivity biomarker as written. (Registry row codes modality_subtype as structural_MRI_only, contradicting the block's rs-fMRI, but the block itself is functional MRI.)

claim: P-607 (Allegretti 2025, Cortex; MCI n=30 accuracy / 21 eye-movement) found the MECHANISMS of object-scene VWM binding preserved in MCI - semantic-inconsistency detection benefit, first-pass gaze-duration benefit, and attentional prioritisation showed no significant group interaction across younger/older/MCI (a null result = no detectable difference, not proven equivalence) - while overall MCI detection accuracy ...
second_reader_note: The P-607 block (title matches Allegretti/Cortex 2025, not misattached) supports the core invalidation: "What are the outcomes?" states semantic-inconsistency prioritisation and fixation-duration benefits held "regardless of age or cognitive impairment", "What are the problems?" confirms "non-significant group interactions" with a "significant OVERALL MCI accuracy deficit", and sample n=30 accuracy / 21 eye-movement matches. However the record's what_disproved_it cites a specific statistic "b=-1.37, p<0.001" for the MCI accuracy deficit that appears nowhere in the block (grep for 1.37 / p<0.001 / b= returns nothing), and the rule makes an uncorroborated number a reject; drop the coefficient (or source it into the block from the PDF) and the record would otherwise be admissible, since the prior is the block's own "generalised-impairment accounts" framing, not a straw man.

claim: P-274 (Arvidsson 2024; BioFINDER-1 SCD/MCI n=332 + external ADNI n=108, longitudinal) benchmarked whole-image deep learning against interpretable clinical/region-based baselines: the DL model did NOT outperform on discrimination (DL AUC 0.84 vs clinical 0.85; difference small and not significance-tested) and was clearly worse on continuous MMSE-slope prediction (R2 0.08 vs 0.14-0.17).
second_reader_note: P-274's block (title: "Comparing a pre-defined versus deep learning approach for extracting brain atrophy patterns...", Arvidsson 2024, matches the cited PMID) reports a within-study null exactly as the record states: "Clinical model: AUC 0.85... R2 0.14", "Clinical + hippocampal volume: AUC 0.86; R2 0.16", "Clinical + regional MRI volumes: AUC 0.83; R2 0.17", "DL model: AUC 0.84; R2 0.08 (worse than simpler region-based baselines)", with "BioFINDER-1 SCD/MCI participants (n=332)" and "ADNI subset (n=108)" as external cohort. The prior is a genuine field assumption the paper itself set out to test ("Many studies assume deep imaging models are superior; this work directly and rigorously tests that assumption"), and the record's clinical_implication already bounds the finding to SCD/MCI on this single cohort family; the only clause not literally in the block is the hedge "not significance-tested", which weakens rather than inflates the claim.

claim: Digital/behavioural biomarkers (speech, language/NLP, spontaneous conversation) detect MCI from non-clinical data across independent cohorts.
second_reader_note: Four listed studies support the statement as written from four dataset families and at least two method families: P-6 (I-CONECT video-interview transcripts, transformer NLP, "distinguished between MCI and NC with an average AUC of 84.75%"), P-58 (spontaneous speech temporal features + SVM on separate English and Hungarian MCI/HC cohorts, 67-92%), P-352 (TAUKADIAL spontaneous speech, "129 train (74 MCI/55 NC)", translingual markers "useful for both binary MCI detection and MMSE estimation"), and weakly P-938 (Dublin conversational speech timing, "MCI-HC contrast 63%", speech slowness characterises MCI). Three listed supporters do not carry the claim and should be pruned rather than counted: P-102 is AD-BERT on EHR clinical notes predicting MCI-to-AD progression (clinical data, not MCI detection); P-276's block never mentions MCI (ADReSS/Turkish "cognitive-impairment severity/MMSE-related status"); P-884's block states "MCI-specific discrimination not reported separately" (only 3-class and HE vs MCI+AD/D). None contradicts the statement; caveat that P-6's sample field reads "77 AD + 74 HC" while its method/findings fields say MCI vs NC on I-CONECT.

claim: Among physical-function measures, performance under load and functional capacity - gait speed, grip strength, dual-task cost - are associated with MCI where the corresponding static or mass-based measure is not.
second_reader_note: Only two of the three listed supporters show the contrast as written: P-644 ("among sarcopenia components only handgrip strength and gait speed - not skeletal muscle index - were associated with MCI"; gait OR 0.16, grip OR 0.97, SMI OR 0.86 p=0.189) and P-665 ("ST-TUG did not differ (17.29 vs 17.60 s; p 0.64) while DT-TUG was prolonged (p 0.012) and DTC increased (p 0.014)"). P-637 is a qualitative PRISMA review whose Key findings field says only that quantitative MCDT "can support MCI stratification, risk prediction" with "no pooled accuracy or effect sizes"; its block contains no single-task-versus-dual-task or static-versus-load comparison, so it does not support the "where the corresponding static or mass-based measure is not" clause, leaving fewer than three supporters (the two remaining are both Chinese cross-sectional classical-statistics cohorts, so a rescope would not reach the three-study threshold either).

claim: P-516 (Guo 2021; single ADNI rs-fMRI cohort, MCI vs HC, N=143 subjects/299 scans): as PCn correlation-network ORDER increased, classification ACCURACY decreased (converging to ~50%/chance at large n; exact metrics figure-only), so escalating order did not improve accuracy over the simple low-order network. Note: the second-order 'correlation's correlation' (PC2) and PCn+PC1 fusion still improved SENSITIVITY - ...
second_reader_note: The P-516 block (Guo et al. 2021, Front. Neurosci., title matches) contains a within-study reversal of the prior: "As the order n increases, the ACC of PCn-based BFNs generally decreases ... when the BFN converges (large n) the ACC approaches 50% (chance)", with "Specific numeric ACC/AUC values are presented only in figures" and sample "143 subjects (299 scans: 145 MCI / 154 HC scans)", all matching the record's numbers and figure-only caveat. The prior is a real field assumption the block itself attributes to prior work (Chen 2016, Zhang 2016 "found PC2 more sensitive to AD/MCI"; the authors' motivation was "whether higher-order correlation produces stronger discriminative ability"), and the record's own bounding note (fusion "generally improves sensitivity (SEN) ... but fails to improve ACC and SPE"; "confirms added (sensitivity) information from PC2") is likewise verbatim-supported, so no rescope is needed.

claim: Every MCI intervention trial and synthesis in this batch reports its result as change on a cognitive rating scale with no anchor to disease course - no conversion endpoint, no functional endpoint measured beyond 30 days, and no biomarker trajectory interpreted in a direction the paper commits to - so a reported MMSE mean difference of 1.63 or a standardised mean difference of 0.57 cannot be translated into any ...
second_reader_note: All quoted numbers match their blocks (P-655 SMD 1.21 and "Conversion to dementia was not among the seven outcomes extracted"; P-641 SMD 0.57, 0.19-0.94, I2 87%; P-642 MD 1.63/2.84; P-649 FSIQ betas 0.107-0.136, lower CI 0.006; P-653 d=0.80/0.64 at 30 days; P-652 MoCA p=0.005 sole of eight; P-628 N=60, MMSE-only) and no listed paper meets the closure criteria, but the statement's clause "no biomarker trajectory interpreted in a direction the paper commits to" is contradicted by the P-628 block, whose Key findings are "a-GPC lowered the annualised rate of hippocampal and entorhinal atrophy and ventricular dilation versus placebo at 12 months" read as "supporting a disease-modifying rationale", and by P-649's plasma Abeta42/ketone/mtDNA-deletion changes reported "in the same participants" as "a coherent biochemical story". Narrower scope that is genuinely open: no MCI intervention trial in the batch reports the within-trial association between its cognitive-scale change and a disease-course endpoint (P-628 gives no magnitudes or link; P-649 is peripheral blood only with no link), none retains a functional endpoint beyond 30 days, and none has a conversion/reversion endpoint; drop or narrow the "no committed-direction biomarker trajectory" clause to "no CNS biomarker trajectory with reported effect magnitudes tied to the cognitive change".

claim: P-452 (EEG/MEG, biomarker analysis): Small sex subsamples; correlational only; single-centre.
second_reader_note: The P-452 block matches its title (sex-stratified rs-EEG spectral signatures vs CSF Abeta42/t-tau/p-tau in MCI) and its "Potential gaps or limitations" field reads verbatim "Small sex subsamples; correlational only; single-centre." (N = 27, 12 F / 15 M, single Lleida cohort, Spearman correlation, V2), so nothing in the record is unsupported and P-452 cannot close its own limitation. As written, however, the statement is a single-study limitation paste with an empty gap_type and a generic closure criterion, not a literature absence; it is admissible only in the narrower form the block supports ("What can be improved? Larger sex-balanced cohorts and predictive validation"; Open Problems: "Whether sex-specific markers improve prediction"): no multi-centre, sex-balanced study with predictive (out-of-sample) validation of sex-specific rs-EEG spectral correlates of CSF AD biomarkers in MCI.

claim: P-103 identifies reproducible longitudinal subphenotypes (respiratory, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic) across independent EHR cohorts
second_reader_note: The P-103 block (dynaPhenoM, 3,952 AD patients, three US EHR cohorts) contains the claimed evidence verbatim: "Identified five progression subphenotypes from MCI to AD", four cross-cohort ones "respiratory, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic", "One subtype (digestive) appeared cohort-specific", and "progression from MCI to AD is not uniform". But the subphenotypes are organ-system comorbidity/medication/procedure topics in US-only EHR data, and the block itself states "Biological causality cannot be established from retrospective EHR trajectories alone", treats heterogeneity as its premise ("MCI-to-AD progression is clinically heterogeneous") and says it "Extends prior AD subtype studies"; so the evidence bounds a uniform-trajectory assumption for the clinical/comorbidity course of MCI-to-AD in EHR-based prognostic modelling, not the general neurocognitive progression pathway, and "directly and strongly disproved" plus "only noise-level inter-patient variation" overstate it. Narrower scope: the assumption that MCI-to-AD clinical trajectories can be modelled as one homogeneous course is contradicted for US EHR cohorts (four reproducible comorbidity-defined subphenotypes), with the prior softened from "single dominant pathway with only noise-level variation" to "uniform clinical course adequate for one-size-fits-all prognosis".

claim: saliency no attention analysis no feature-importance ranking beyond the variable-combination search itself
second_reader_note: The P-788 block contains no brain-scan evidence at all ("No MRI, fMRI, DTI, PET or any other scan acquisition or analysis is described anywhere in the extracted text"; C1 rejected, registry Modality C5): the study's only within-study comparison is clinical scales (RPDPM on Lawton/MMSE/CDT, AUC 0.945) versus plasma p-tau181 (AUC 0.57, CI 0.39-0.74), so it cannot bound a prior about brain scans, and the lone imaging mention is a discussion remark that other DPMs "typically use magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography, cerebrospinal fluid and blood biomarkers", not a result. The what_disproved_it field is a truncated slice of the block's XAI-absence sentence ("no saliency, no attention analysis, no feature-importance ranking beyond the variable-combination search itself"), which describes the absence of an explainability method and is not evidence against any prior; the "categorically superior" prior is also a straw man. Not rescope, because the paper's real null (plasma p-tau181 in the oldest old) concerns a different predictor class, not a narrower setting of the stated brain-scan prior.

claim: Across >=4 independent MCI intervention classes (non-invasive brain stimulation, exercise, cognitive training, nutrition), pooled efficacy estimates are large but statistically fragile - built on few small trials, extreme heterogeneity (I^2 ~ 65-98%), non-interchangeable outcome scales pooled as unit-free SMDs, and biologically implausible magnitudes (up to Hedges g ~ 5.6) - so no stable, harmonised, credible effect ...
second_reader_note: None of the seven blocks is a meta-analysis or contains any pooled estimate, I^2, SMD or Hedges g: P-914 "Best Metric: Qualitative ... no pooled metric" and "no pooled estimates"; P-916 "Best Metric: ... modest cognitive benefits of 40 Hz interventions; no pooled metric"; P-921 (n=31 pre-post IVR pilot), P-968 (n=24 magic RCT), P-972 (n=130 probiotic RCT) and P-987 (n=38 pre-post app study) are single primary trials, and P-929 is a retrospective cholinesterase-inhibitor cohort, not one of the four named intervention classes. The record's core numbers ("I^2 ~ 65-98%", "Hedges g ~ 5.6", unit-free SMDs, cross-intervention rankings) appear in no block, and P-987's only meta-analytic mention ("Lampit 2020 meta-analysis (90 trials) found small global-cognition effects") runs against the "pooled efficacy estimates are large" premise, so zero of seven listed studies support the statement as written.

claim: Within ADNI, neuropsychological features consistently outrank imaging in direct comparisons (P-243, P-48, P-320), but this pattern has NOT been verified in non-ADNI cohorts.
second_reader_note: The three listed supporters are all ADNI MCI-conversion studies and each shows the direction: P-81 "Cognitive scores alone outperformed PET alone" (3D CNN, N=612); P-243 "LASSO feature selection eliminates MRI features in favor of neuropsychological tests", top predictors FAQ/mPACCtrailsB/RAVLT/ADAS11 (ensemble ML, N=627); P-48 "neuropsychological plus AD-related biomarkers" ~0.90 Acc vs "sMRI-only ... about 0.79" (tree ensembles, N=587). But the statement cannot be admitted as written: (1) its parenthetical cites P-320, whose block is a private Baskent-hospital EEG study ("ADNI is not mentioned", Assigned ADNI Dependent: false, no neuropsychological features), so that attribution is unsupported and must be replaced by P-81; (2) only one dataset family (ADNI, overlapping MCI samples), so the required >1 dataset family is unmet; (3) "consistently outrank in direct comparisons" overstates P-48 (winner is neuropsych+CSF/APOE, not neuropsych alone, and hippocampal atrophy was still an important predictor) and P-243 (a LASSO feature-selection outcome, not a modality-vs-modality model comparison); only P-81 is a clean cognitive-only vs imaging-only comparison. Narrower scope: "In three ADNI MCI-to-AD conversion studies (P-243, P-48, P-81; not P-320), cognitive-score feature sets outperformed imaging-only models or displaced MRI features under feature selection; P-48's winning set combined cognition with CSF/APOE biomarkers; all draw on overlapping ADNI MCI samples and no non-ADNI r

claim: Two physically distinct non-volumetric contrasts - functional connectivity and tissue mechanics - each access an aMCI signal precisely where standard volumetry is silent, indicating a volume-negative MCI is not marker-negative and that functional and mechanical channels are non-redundant.
second_reader_note: finding_a is an empty string, so the admit condition (each finding supported by its own block) cannot be met as submitted; the P-518 block does contain the intended finding ("Hippocampal subvolumes ... did NOT differentiate HC from mdaMCI ... significant global decoupling of frontal-temporal and temporal-occipital regions in mdaMCI vs HC", N=44, 24 HC/14 mdaMCI/6 mAD) and finding_b matches P-478 exactly (N=83, 20 aMCI/63 CN, "Lower DG-CA3 mu predicted aMCI regardless of DG-CA3 volume", "combined ROC AUC=0.85", "detects aMCI even when volume is preserved"). Narrower scope: (1) populate finding_a from the P-518 block; (2) drop "functional and mechanical channels are non-redundant" - neither study measured both channels, so mutual non-redundancy is untested and only non-redundancy with volumetry is shown; (3) "precisely where standard volumetry is silent" overstates P-478, where volume alone still gave AUC 0.77 and stiffness was additive/volume-independent rather than a signal in a volume-silent setting; (4) note the cohorts differ (mdaMCI vs generic aMCI, group-difference T4 vs classification T1).

claim: The NMA ranking does not robustly support multi-ingredient superiority over omega-3: the significant Multi arm rests on N=526 vs the null Omega-3 arm's N=2293 with an implausible ~2-SD effect (small-study/precision-asymmetry pattern). This undercuts the reliability of the ranking; it does not by itself establish omega-3 superiority or multi-ingredient ineffectiveness.
second_reader_note: The P-151 block (Key findings reported) supports only "52 trials with 8452 participants ... the multi-ingredient intervention outperformed other interventions significantly (SMD 2.03; 95% CrI 0.97-3.09)"; it contains no omega-3 arm, no "N=526" or "N=2293", no null result and no small-study/precision-asymmetry finding, so the entire what_disproved_it is a reader's re-analysis absent from the block. The "prior belief" is also framed as this single paper's own ranking conclusion rather than a field-level assumption, and the block reports no within-study null or reversal.

claim: The same astrocytic protein (GFAP) moves in OPPOSITE directions across two biofluids in the corpus: plasma GFAP rises with AD pathology (P-54 and the wider plasma-GFAP literature) while salivary GFAP falls in MCI/AD (P-1234). This compartment-specific direction conflict is invisible from either paper alone - P-1234 has no blood comparison and P-54 has no saliva - and has direct measurement implications: a ...
second_reader_note: The combined insight is stated by P-1234 alone: its block says "GFAP direction is opposite to plasma GFAP literature (decreased in saliva vs increased in plasma)" (What are the problems?), "increased GFAP in plasma and brain in AD contrasts with the salivary decrease, suggesting compartment-specific regulation" (Related findings), and proposes "comparison with plasma GFAP in the same subjects" (What can be improved?), which is exactly the record's clinical_implication; the record's claim that the conflict is "invisible from either paper alone - P-1234 has no blood comparison" misreads that block. Finding_a's numbers (N=60, 13.35/6.82/3.56 ng/mg, J=0.95, sens 95%/spec 100%) match P-1234, but finding_b overstates P-54: the block never states plasma GFAP is "ELEVATED" in MCI (only "cognitive scores negatively correlated with plasma biomarkers"), reports AUCs "in approximately 0.78-0.93 range" rather than a flat 0.93, and the "broader plasma-GFAP literature" clause is imported from outside the block.

claim: P-142 (MIND-China, N=1072 dementia-free; 243 SCD, 246 MCI) found via VBM that MCI had reduced GMV in bilateral parahippocampus, hippocampus, and fusiform, while SCD showed no significant GMV difference from normal cognition (P>0.05). However, the SAME study's ROI-wise SBM analysis found SCD WAS significantly associated with cortical thinning in the right paracentral sulcus, left caudal middle frontal gyrus, and left ...
second_reader_note: The block's "Key findings reported" confirms N=1072, 243 SCD/246 MCI, and the VBM result ("MCI ... reduced GMV in ... bilateral para-hippocampus, bilateral hippocampus, and bilateral fusiform (P D0.05), but SCD exhibited no significant differences with normal cognition in GMV (P F0.05)"), but it truncates at "The ROI-wise SBM analysis revealed that SCD was significantly associated with " so the record's SBM specifics (cortical thinning in right paracentral sulcus, left caudal middle frontal gyrus, left entorhinal cortex, P<0.05) are not in the block. More fundamentally the record does not present an invalidation: its own clinical_implication states "The prior belief ... is therefore NOT invalidated", and the only in-block null (VBM GMV) is absorbed by the prior's "detectable with sensitive enough methods" clause while the same block confirms SBM did find a significant SCD association. A VBM-only bound could arguably be rescoped, but the record as written asserts no invalidated assumption and carries region-level claims the block cannot verify.

claim: P-50 (VBM+SBM, N=46) and P-99 (FreeSurfer Random Forest, N=207) show MCI structural change is DISTRIBUTED, not hippocampus-confined. P-50 reports significant volume reductions not only in hippocampus (left p=0.006, right p=0.008) but also thalamus (left p=0.011), pallidum (right p=0.009) and amygdala (left p=0.031), plus cortical sulcal-depth and gyrification changes (fusiform, parahippocampal, lingual, ...
second_reader_note: The P-50 block supports the substance (Results: "atrophy in left thalamus/hippocampus/amygdala, right pallidum/hippocampus", "shallower left-hemisphere sulcal depth and increased right frontal gyrification", "Combined cortical+subcortical features achieved about 89%"; Significance: "Supports distributed gray-matter structural disruption"), but what_disproved_it adds five p-values (0.006/0.008/0.011/0.009/0.031) and four named cortical regions (fusiform, parahippocampal, lingual, orbitofrontal) that appear nowhere in the block; grep of the block for any p-value or those gyri returns nothing. P-99 (N=207 matches) lists "Volume increases in Lateral Ventricle, Inferior Lateral Ventricle, CSF; volume decreases in Amygdala, Hippocampus, Accumbens" but attributes feature selection to chi-squared SelectKBest, not "Random Forest weights". Numbers and region claims not in the block make this a reject as written; a rewrite confined to the block's regions, the 89% joint-feature result and the corrected P-99 attribution would be supportable (the prior, hippocampus-only structural profiling, is a real field practice, though neither block gives a within-study hippocampus-alone comparison).

claim: In both the white-matter (tract sub-bundle) and gray-matter (cortical minicolumn) compartments, fine-grained diffusion sub-metrics unlock diagnostic/prognostic signal invisible to coarse whole-tract or macro-volumetric summaries - granularity, not modality, is the differentiator.
second_reader_note: finding_b is fully supported (P-581 Key findings: "Cortical diffusivity (PerpPD+ ...) outperforms hippocampal volume, cortical volume, and cortical thickness in Kaplan-Meier survival", N=826 NACC). finding_a matches P-408 on N=60 NACC, parietal tracts and "occipital tracts are relatively spared", but the block only says sub-tracts are "potentially better than whole-splenium metrics" (Significance; Results reports no whole-splenium comparison), so "whole-splenium metrics ... relatively uninformative" is stronger than the block. The combined insight overreaches on "invisible to coarse ... summaries" (both blocks report outperformed/potentially better, not absent signal) and on "granularity, not modality, is the differentiator" (P-581's contrast is diffusion microstructure vs T1-derived volume/thickness, i.e. cross-measure, while P-408 is within-DTI parcellation). Narrower scope that holds jointly and is stated by neither alone: in both white matter (P-408, T1 diagnosis, in-sample AUC 0.75 MCI-vs-HC, n=20/group) and cortex (P-581, T2 prognosis, KM survival), finer-grained diffusion measures outperformed coarser comparators (hedged whole-splenium metrics; macrostructural volume/thickness).

claim: P-49 studied dynamic functional connectivity states in 82 MCI patients and 85 controls using rs-fMRI. The paper identified three distinct DFC states. Crucially, State 2 showed no significant community structure differences between MCI and controls — it was the state with highest DMN-like activity. The significant MCI-related disruptions were concentrated in States 1 and 3, affecting frontal, temporal, and ...
second_reader_note: The P-49 block never mentions the DMN or default mode network (grep of the block returns no hit), so the record's load-bearing claims that State 2 "was the state with highest DMN-like activity" and that disruptions fell "rather than the DMN core" are not in the block; the block's Results field instead lists "frontal, temporal, occipital/precuneus-related nodes" as differential regions, and precuneus is a DMN hub, which cuts against the record's reading. The cohort numbers (82 MCI/85 controls, N=167, three DFC states, State 2 no significant difference, States 1 and 3 altered) do match, but what the block supports is "MCI disruptions are state-specific", which is not evidence against DMN dominance; the prior as phrased ("detectable across all patients and all dynamic states") is also a straw-man extension no one holds.

claim: Study A (P-41): P-41: Multi-view 2D projection ensemble — AUC ~0.92 on T2 (sMCI→pMCI/AD), ADNI internal (V2) validation || Study B (P-65): P-65: 3D hemispheric asymmetry CNN — AUC ~0.84 on T2 (MCI→AD), ADNI internal (V2) validation
second_reader_note: Both blocks match the claims: P-41 "Outcomes" reports "92% AUC" on ADNI for sMCI-to-pMCI/AD progression using three MRI planes (axial/coronal/sagittal) with 2D backbones (EfficientNet-B7/ConvNeXt/DenseNet-121) in an ensemble, ADNI-only evaluation ("without extensive external-site validation"); P-65 reports "AUC 84.01%" on ADNI ("Cross-validation on ADNI") for MCI-to-AD conversion (300 pMCI/273 sMCI) with a 3D hemispheric-asymmetry CNN, and the registry codes both as T2 / structural_MRI_only / ADNI / V2, so task, modality family, dataset family and validation tier agree and 0.92 - 0.8401 = 0.08 as claimed. Caveats that do not trip any reject condition: P-41's block does not spell out its internal validation scheme (V2 comes from the registry), neither block states a conversion horizon, and P-41's sample line is internally inconsistent (192 vs 96+81=177).

claim: Study A (P-190): P-190: Acc 90.62 on T2 || Study B (P-192): P-192: PPV 68.0 on T2
second_reader_note: The two numbers are different metric types: P-190 reports "accuracy 90.62 +/- 1.16%" (SVM on FDG-PET deep radiomics + clinical, 3-year MCI-c/MCI-nc, repeated 10-fold CV, registry primary_metric_type=Accuracy) while P-192's figure is a prevalence-dependent PPV ("RUSBoost PPV ... about 68% vs 22.2% [observed base rate] at 4 years", registry Best_Metric and primary_metric_type both "not reported"), so a 0.226 gap between Acc and PPV is not a contradiction. The modality families also differ (P-190 modality_subtype=PET imaging radiomics; P-192 Modality="ATN biomarkers" profile cut-offs vs continuous-feature models) and neither is the record's "clinical_survey"; horizons differ (3.0 vs 4 years for the 68% figure) and P-192 is coded survival_analysis. Apparent disagreement only.

claim: Subjective concern signals and conversational NLP can be fused into remote-first early detection workflows
second_reader_note: P-108 block supports SCCs as prospective low-cost risk signals ("Achievable Outcomes: Better risk stratification using low-cost subjective data"; both self- and informant-SCC RRs significant) and its "What can be improved" calls for "Integration with objective biomarkers and digital markers", which P-6 supplies (transformer NLP on video-interview transcripts, "average Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 84.75%", "Automated, affordable screening for MCI"), so the fusion inference is a genuine joint insight stated by neither alone. Narrower scope: drop "remote-first" (neither block mentions remote delivery), reword finding_b from "risk scoring" to diagnostic MCI-vs-NC classification (P-6 is cross-sectional, not prognostic), and strike "increase case-finding sensitivity" from the implication because no block tests or claims a sensitivity gain from combining the two signals.

claim: MCI case status is operationalised at least four incompatible ways across this corpus - ICD-10 registry code, single screening-instrument threshold, brief composite cognitive score, and consensus neuropsychological criteria - producing frequency estimates that differ by more than an order of magnitude in the same disease, yet no study applies two or more definitions to the SAME cohort to quantify how much of an ...
second_reader_note: Every number checks: P-648 "MCI was defined by ICD-10 codes G31.8, R41 and F06.7 ... 1797 (1.4 %) developed MCI" in 126,785 over median 13.0 y; P-650 "3272 developed incident MCI" in 200,726 (~1.6%, mean 13.1 y); P-644 education-stratified MMSE + CDRS + IADL, 17.3%; P-639 MoCA-J <= 25, 65.2%; P-656 NIA-AA algorithmic, 153/337 = 45.4%; P-646 HRS composite "equating of MCI with memory loss"; P-651 "MCI inclusion rule specified MMSE between 24 and 26 ... CSVD-MCI mean of 27.86 +/- 2.15 ... F 2.461, P 0.089"; P-654 lists eight criteria, "only 14 studies used CT or MRI", I2 = 98.03%, with subgroups on sample source/sleep-measurement method/region/design and meta-regression on year/age/sex/quality only; P-657 "28 studies diagnosed MCI by Petersen criteria and 7 by Winblad ... I-squared = 98.4%" with six subgroups (age, gender, design, referral source, region, StD ascertainment) - so no listed paper applies two MCI definitions to one cohort or enters MCI ascertainment as a moderator, and the closure criteria are concrete and MCI-specific. Two evidence-text overstatements should be softened but do not affect the verdict: P-650's block files the ICD under-capture as a summariser-added limitation ("Beyond these"), not author-acknowledged; and neither synthesis block names MCI-criteria heterogeneity the "prime suspect" (P-654 attributes it mainly to aetiological diversity, P-657 partly to I2 sensitivity and the broad StD construct), though both list criteria variation and P-656/P-657 ca

claim: No papers found for modality-task combination: Molecular × T6
second_reader_note: The gap_statement "No papers found for modality-task combination: Molecular x T6" is a taxonomy-grid cell with papers_claiming_gap = ["UNRESOLVED"] and evidence "Taxonomy coverage sweep found zero papers" -- a keyword-combination artefact, not an MCI research question -- and the absence is false against the corpus: data/full_paper_registry.csv has 40 C3 (Molecular/Fluid) rows with Task_Type T6, and the blocks confirm it, e.g. P-1341 "Neurofilament light chain in cerebrospinal fluid or blood as a biomarker for mild cognitive impairment: A systematic review and meta-analysis" declares "Assigned: C3 Molecular/Fluid" and "Assigned: T6 Review", and P-1202 (CSF HPA-axis hormones systematic review in MCI/AD) declares "Assigned: C3 Molecular/Fluid" and "Assigned: T6 systematic review"; P-792 and P-908 likewise declare C3 with T6. The closure_criteria ("at least one validated paper covering this modality-task pair") is already met, so the cell is closed, not open.

claim: Within this corpus, every retinal/ocular paper measures retinal STRUCTURE (OCT layer thickness, OCTA vessel density, choroidal thickness); no CORPUS paper uses retinal FUNCTIONAL electrophysiology (full-field / pattern / multifocal ERG) as input features to an ML model for MCI. CORPUS-SAMPLING gap, not a field gap: clinical ERG-for-AD is a real literature (Parisi 2010; Sen 2021).
second_reader_note: None of the four listed blocks closes the gap: P-163 (OCT GC-IPL/OCTA CNN, AUC ~0.81), P-255 (colour-fundus vessel width/AV ratio/tortuosity/fractal dimension, logistic regression, AUC 0.73), P-363 (EDI-OCT SFCT/TCA/LA/CVI with GEE) are all retinal-structure papers and P-105 is an eye-tracking review, so the ML-input closure criterion ("ERG as input features to an ML model for MCI ... reporting AUC/accuracy") is unmet. However the statement's wider premise ("every retinal/ocular paper measures retinal STRUCTURE"; evidence: "'ERG' returns ZERO corpus hits") is no longer true of summaries.md: P-933 records "flash electroretinogram (FERG)" with "delayed rod-cone response latency in both MCI (P=0.003) and AD" in 23 MCI/19 NC/17 AD using ANOVA/hierarchical regression, Best AUC "not reported", and P-830 is a systematic review pooling "PERG (k = 2, n = 72)" for MCI vs CN. Narrower open form: no corpus paper feeds ERG (full-field/pattern/multifocal) into an ML classifier for MCI detection/conversion with AUC/accuracy; drop the "structure-only corpus / zero ERG hits" clause and cite P-933/P-830 as non-closing functional-ERG papers (statistics-only, no classifier).

claim: How MCI status and its correlates are ascertained is a first-order determinant of the reported estimate, not a second-order nuisance: within the same condition, the measurement source and the case definition move prevalence estimates by a factor of two or more, and this dominates every substantive moderator tested alongside it.
second_reader_note: Only P-1046 supports the statement as written (Key findings: "MCI detection 0.062-0.079 (~92% undiagnosed)", a >10x claims-vs-expected gap that dwarfs the race contrast 0.039 vs 0.098), and P-654 supports it only partly (Key findings: "self-reported 49.4% versus informant-rated 23.7%" = 2.08x, but the same field gives region Q = 34.025 > measurement-method Q = 30.173 and a wider 19.1%-45.2% spread, so dominance is not shown). Three listed studies contradict the quantifiers with their own numbers: P-657 (ascertainment "DSM-based 21.3% ... versus 28.9%" = 1.36x, while referral source 36.2% vs 21.6% is the larger moderator), P-955 ("MCI rates 44% (consensus), 53% (actuarial), 41% (LCA)" = 1.29x) and P-971 ("MCI prevalence +9.2% (272 vs 249)"); the remaining seven (P-648, P-650, P-924, P-926, P-937, P-962, P-982) contain no measurement-source-vs-prevalence contrast at all (UK Biobank risk-factor cohorts, RCI/SRB change studies, cross-dataset progression rates, a single MoCA<25 cut-off). Fewer than three supporters and direct contradictions mean reject; a weakened claim (ascertainment method is a significant but variably sized moderator, 1.1x to >10x) could draw on P-654/657/955/971/1046 but is a different statement, not a narrower scope of this one.

claim: P-193 (Cerebral hemodynamics, MCI detection): Sample size and model-form assumptions limit immediate clinical generalization.
second_reader_note: P-193 block (Marmarelis et al. 2021, Frontiers in Physiology, title-consistent) states "### Potential gaps or limitations: Sample size and model-form assumptions limit immediate clinical generalization" verbatim, with N=48 (36 aMCI/12 NC), Laguerre linear dynamic modeling, and "What can be improved: Larger cohorts with external replication; Nonlinear model extensions and mechanistic validation; Integration with imaging/clinical progression endpoints"; registry row confirms modality Cerebral hemodynamics, T1, V2, N=48. As written the statement is a restated single-study limitation with boilerplate closure criteria and empty gap_type, trivially true of any n=48 study rather than an absence; it is open only in the narrower form: no external replication in a larger cohort, no nonlinear-model evaluation, and no longitudinal progression-endpoint linkage of NIRS-derived dynamic cortical-oxygenation (CTO-EtCO2/ABP/CBFV) physio-markers for MCI detection. P-193 itself (the only listed paper) does not close that narrower form.

claim: Depression is entered into MCI models as a dichotomy at a scale cut-off in every corpus study that models it as an exposure, yet the two studies that DO stratify by severity both find the milder stratum carrying the worse biology and the worse trajectory - so the assumed monotone severity-risk relation has never been tested against a continuous or multi-stratum specification. MANDATORY GENERALISATION CAVEAT ...
second_reader_note: The P-643/P-645/P-647/P-657 numbers all match their blocks, but the absence is overstated: P-646's block states "Sensitivity analyses used continuous CES-D and cognitive scores in multilevel growth-curve models" (so the authors did act on the dichotomisation limitation, contradicting the nearest_miss text and "every corpus study ... dichotomy"), and P-656's block reports a dimensional analysis of a continuous SCID symptom count (RR 1.11 per symptom) with "natural cubic splines (df = 3) tested against linear models by nested F-test ... no evidence of non-linearity", which the record omits when it says no corpus study fits severity continuously or tests non-monotonicity. Neither closes the closure criteria (P-646 fits no shape test; P-656 is cross-sectional and its count pools PTSD and MDE symptoms), so the gap is open only in the narrower form: no study models a depression-specific severity measure continuously or in >=3 ordered strata against an MCI biomarker or longitudinal outcome AND formally tests non-linearity; P-663's Personal Distress is an IRI empathy subscale, not depression severity, and should be dropped as a "third inversion".

claim: The MCI / conversion OUTCOME LABEL is operationalised non-comparably across studies - conversion defined over inconsistent and frequently unreported minimum-follow-up windows (2/3/4/8 yr or unstated), contaminating the 'stable' negative class with right-censored future converters; and prevalent-MCI defined by different criteria (MoCA<25, age-standardised MMSE, education-stratified Petersen, EHR/ICD code, ...
second_reader_note: All 13 blocks confirm the window/criterion heterogeneity as stated (P-507 "2-year conversion window", P-3 "within 3 years"/74.61%/593, P-512 "48-month"/"some currently stable patients may convert later", P-88 "8-year follow-up", P-41 "Labeling/progression-window definitions can influence apparent performance" with no window, P-96 "MMSE... age-standardized norms" AUROC 0.93, P-258 "MoCA... <25" AUC 0.8704, P-270 "Petersen criteria with MMSE thresholds by education level" AUC 0.75, P-293 "MCI definitions differed across cohorts"/"Standardize MCI definitions", P-646 "constant redefinition of MCI may explain heterogeneity"), and every paper fits under a single label: P-293 co-varies cohort and definition, P-512's 12-month stratification evaluates one fitted model without relabel/refit or SHAP, P-646 is a T4 hazard-ratio study, so none closes the within-cohort label-only ablation. Two peripheral inexactitudes in evidence_for_open_status only: P-165's block says AUC "around upper-0.6 range" not 0.65, and "education is the dominant predictor" rests on an unreadable VF cross-reference while P-270 names age as strongest splitter and P-96 grip strength/creatinine; declared task_type T2 is also under-inclusive since the criterion facet grounds on T1 screening papers.
